title: Deletion, tombstones and collision reconciliation
summary: Carry deletions safely and reconcile identity collisions without resurrecting or silently discarding records.

specReferences.heading: W7 · Deletion, tombstones and collision reconciliation

conditions: Absence alone never deletes a record.
Detach and reattach cannot resurrect a deleted record.
Reconciliation rewrites every affected reference safely.
completion.summary: Pending tombstone publication, publication-marker forfeiture, natural-key collision reconciliation, aliases, and causal reference rewrites are implemented and guarded at the storage and coordinator boundaries.
evidence: packages/compendium_core/test/sync/sync_merge_test.dart and app/test/sync/sync_coordinator_test.dart cover omission as non-deletion, explicit tombstones, live/publication snapshot separation, baseline exclusion for pending addresses, and post-apply publication.

packages/compendium_core/test/storage/sync_local_repository_test.dart covers epoch reset preserving pending deletions and published records, archive restore revalidation, detach clearing pending state without clearing publication history, and transactional rollback of the coupled state.

packages/compendium_core/test/storage/sync_storage_test.dart and app/test/sync/sync_coordinator_test.dart cover cited tombstones, pending tombstone overlay publication, final-citation application, deliberate restore versus archive restore, marker-before-manifest publication, and unavailable-peer alias retention.

packages/compendium_core/test/storage/sync_publication_lifecycle_test.dart covers published-record tombstoning through choreographer, tag, published-source, custom-field, difficulty, venue, dance, program, and shareable-settings permanent-delete paths.

packages/compendium_core/test/storage/sync_local_repository_test.dart covers transitive alias resolution, fixed-point alias remapping, publication-marker union from a transitive loser, peer-manifest alias retirement, and marker preservation across reset and detach.

packages/compendium_core/test/storage/sync_storage_test.dart covers both natural-key survivor directions, existence/content separation, equal-time body review, known-UUID rename review, malformed-collision isolation, shipped difficulty-ID canonicalization, custom-field type mismatch retention, deterministic short/full suffix escalation, and occupied-suffix review termination.

packages/compendium_core/test/storage/sync_storage_test.dart covers local author, tag, custom-field, and difficulty reference rewrites; the all-kind inbound-reference guard proves that losing IDs are rewritten before foreign-key validation and commit.

packages/compendium_core/test/storage/sync_storage_test.dart covers same-batch natural-key collisions, deterministic same-batch custom-field type suffixing, pending tombstone migration across an identity remap, and causal stamping of inbound bodies changed by aliases.
The all-kind inbound-reference guard was run with the tag rewrite removed from rewriteSyncInboundReferences and went red with an unresolved-reference report; restoring the rewrite made it green.

The device-local custom-field guard was first shown ineffective when only writeFromSyncParent was mutated; mutating the actual writeFromSyncRelations boundary to preserveDeviceLocalCustomFields: false went red because the stored dance lost one of two expected fields, and restoring both sync writers made it green.

The alias remap guard was strengthened to mark only the transitive loser; replacing the remap fixed-point loop with one pass went red because the survivor lacked the transitive publication marker, and restoring the loop made it green.
The local-reference I1 guard asserts a strict updated_at advance and changed publication wire hash; omitting the causal bump was run red and the restored implementation passed.
The renamed custom-field I1 guard asserts the renamed definition's causal timestamp and publication body; omitting that bump was run red and the restored implementation passed.

The repaired review guards cover coordinator alias normalization, deterministic natural-key survivor selection, private/shareable custom-field isolation, canonical difficulty known-UUID review, transitive alias-chain retention, and causal timestamp advancement for remapped pending tombstones; each was run red before restoration.

The final review guards `a cached aliased blob with the wrong envelope is rejected` and `aliased natural-key reconciliation rejects a changed local survivor` were run red after mutating cached identity checks to alias-resolved comparison and removing the post-alias expected-wire-hash guard; both failed as expected and were restored from commit 10f9150e643a4439c0fcd15167af865c5561ac80.

Mutation runs were completed and restored for pending exclusion, final-citation revalidation, existence/content separation, known-UUID review, custom-field suffix derivation and escalation, canonical difficulty IDs, publication-marker union, hard-delete protection, reset/detach lifecycle, alias retirement, and both collision survivor directions.

python3 tools/preflight.py completed with 30 steps passed and 0 skipped, including sync invariants, privacy and persisted-field ratchets, changelog checks, fixtures, formatting, analysis, core/app/server tests, and benchmark checks.
